awareness.name: Unaware
awareness.text: Busy with its work. Does not activate or react. Becomes Alerted when its element sees a player model, hears noise, is hit, or the alarm is raised.

awareness.name: Alerted
awareness.text: Knows something is wrong but has no target in sight. Activates using its profile's No target list, toward the marker.

awareness.name: Engaged
awareness.text: Any Alerted model that can see a standing player model when it activates or reacts. Uses its profile's Target in sight list.

awareness.name: At the start
awareness.text: Elements start Unaware unless the mission says otherwise. Automated models, and models the mission places on Overwatch, start Alerted.

marker: Place or move the marker to the source of the latest noise, or to where an enemy model last saw a player model.
An Alerted model that ends a Move within 3" of the marker, seeing no player model, removes it. Its element then holds where it is.
With no marker on the board, Alerted models hold: stay in cover facing the nearest approach and go on Overwatch.
alarm: When an element first sees a player model or is hit, it raises the alarm at the end of its next activation: every element on the board becomes Alerted, and the alert track rises by 1.
If every model of the element is Down, Dead or has surrendered before then, the alarm is not raised.

noise.name: Quiet
noise.sources: Moving, opening and closing doors, hacking, close combat, Silenced shots, smoke grenades

noise.name: Loud
noise.sources: Unsilenced shooting, forcing a door with a breaching tool
noise.heard: Elements with a model within 12" aboard ship, measured through walls; within 24" on land

noise.name: Very loud
noise.sources: Frag grenades, flashbangs, breaching charges, any explosion

drills.name: No drill
drills.text: Each model follows its lists alone. Shoots instead of Aiming, never cracks doors, and throws grenades only where its list says.

drills.name: Fire and manoeuvre
drills.text: A model ends a Move in the open, in sight of a player model, only while a friend of its element covers it: on Overwatch, or Engaged with the same target. Otherwise it stops in the last cover on its route, or goes on Overwatch instead of moving. Charges are exempt.

drills.name: Bounding and grenades
drills.text: As Regular, and: throws a frag at 2 or more player models within its explosion radius, with no friend in it; at a closed door (aboard ship or into a building) with the marker or a seen player model beyond, cracks and throws (flashbang first, else frag); the last model of the element to activate each round goes on Overwatch if it has no target.

drills.name: Assault drill
drills.text: As Veteran, and: focus fire, shooting the player model its element has already hit this round if it can see it; picks Leaders and Auto gunners first at each step of the target list.

activation_order: A Leader with a friend within 6" that has 2 or more Suppression.
Other Engaged models, most Suppression first.
Alerted models, nearest the marker first.
targets: Ignore Down, Dead and surrendered models unless nothing else is in sight.
A player model it can hit without a cover penalty, nearest first.
Otherwise the player model in the least cover, nearest first.
Auto weapons spread to every other player model they can engage.
moving: To cover: the nearest position in cover within the Move, Heavy before Light. If the line says "with a target", it must still see one; otherwise it ends out of sight of every player model if it can.

Toward the marker or a target: by the shortest route (through doors aboard ship or in buildings; on land, from cover to cover where the route allows), ending in cover if it can. Enemy models open locked doors on their own vessel or ground with an Interact.
Away: by the shortest route out of sight of every player model, ending in cover.
close_quarters: Used first by an Engaged model with a player model within 6", unless its profile says otherwise. Read top-down.
Outnumbered (more standing player models than friends within 6" of it) and not Aggressive: Move away, then Shoot if it still has a target.
Fight 2 or more, a target within its Move, and Aggressive or Tactical: charge it (close combat).
Two or more player models within a frag's explosion radius of one point, no friend in it, and it carries frag: Throw it, then Move to cover.
Otherwise: use its profile's Target in sight list.
surrender: A model whose profile allows it tests when it activates Pinned or Wounded with a player model within 6" in its line of sight: 2d6 + Nerve, 8+, or it surrenders.
A surrendered model lies down, takes no actions, cannot react and is not a target. It is a prisoner if the mission allows it.
tie_breakers: The option nearest the enemy's objective, or the marker if there is no objective.
The lowest-numbered enemy model, or the player model nearest the enemy's objective.

terms.text: Where a model is: a compartment, passage or junction aboard ship; on land, a building, a terrain piece, or the open ground between them.
A way an enemy can come into a model's area: a door aboard ship; a door or window of a building; on land, the side of the model's cover that faces the marker.
The entry point the mission gives the enemy, a secondary airlock or escape pod aboard ship, or the enemy's board edge on land.

behaviors.name: Cowed
behaviors.summary: Holds its ground, falls back under Suppression, may surrender.
behaviors.investigate: None. Cowed models never move toward the marker.
engaged: Pinned or Wounded, with a player model within 6" in sight: test to surrender, then carry on down the list if it passes.
In the open: Move to cover, then Move away.
Otherwise: Shoot, Shoot.
alerted: If it can see an approach toward the marker: Move away, out of sight of that approach.
reactions: Unactivated: when shot at in the open, Move to cover.

behaviors.name: Sentry
behaviors.summary: Holds chokepoints, overwatches approaches, raises the alarm.
behaviors.investigate: One model: the lowest-numbered model without an Auto weapon. The rest hold.
engaged: In the open: Move to cover with a target, then Shoot.
Auto weapon with two or more targets in sight: Suppressive Fire, then Shoot.
A target within short range: Aim, then Shoot.
Otherwise: Shoot, then Overwatch.
alerted: The investigator: Move toward the marker, twice.
Already in cover covering the approach to its area nearest the marker: Overwatch.
Others: Move to cover covering that approach, then Overwatch.
reactions: Overwatch: Shoot at the first trigger it can.
Unactivated: when shot at in the open, Move to cover.
behaviors.close_combat: Breaks after a lost exchange if Wounded or with 2 or more Suppression.

behaviors.name: Aggressive
behaviors.summary: Closes distance, flanks through side passages, seeks close combat.
engaged: Fight 2 or more and a target within its Move: charge it.
A target within short range: Shoot, Shoot.
Otherwise: Move toward the nearest target, then Shoot.
alerted: Move toward the marker, twice. Prefer a route that does not pass through a door or open ground a player model can see (flanking).
reactions: Overwatch: Shoot at the first trigger it can.
Unactivated: when a player model comes within short range in its sight, Shoot.
behaviors.close_combat: Never breaks while it has fewer than 3 Suppression.

behaviors.name: Tactical
behaviors.summary: Fire and manoeuvre: one element fixes while another moves; uses Overwatch and grenades.
behaviors.investigate: Every model, in bounds: the first model to activate Moves, the next covers it from Overwatch, alternating.
engaged: In the open: Move to cover with a target, then Shoot.
No friend of its element is covering the target: Shoot, then Overwatch.
A friend is covering and the target is beyond short range: Move to cover closer to the target, out of its line of sight on the way if it can, then Shoot.
Otherwise: Aim, then Shoot.
alerted: First of its element this round: Move toward the marker, then Overwatch.
Otherwise: Move to cover covering the friend ahead, then Overwatch.
reactions: Overwatch: Shoot at the first trigger it can.
Unactivated: when shot at in the open, Move to cover; when a player model comes within short range in its sight, Shoot.
behaviors.close_combat: Breaks after a lost exchange if Wounded or with 2 or more Suppression.

behaviors.name: Saboteur
behaviors.summary: Avoids fights; works consoles, rigs charges, seals doors, destroys evidence.
behaviors.investigate: None. Saboteurs work their task and seal doors.
engaged: Pinned or Wounded, with a player model within 6" in sight: test to surrender, then carry on down the list if it passes.
Within 1" of its task: Interact (the mission says what each Interact achieves), then Interact again.
In the open: Move away, then Throw smoke between itself and the target if it has one.
Otherwise: Shoot, then Move away.
alerted: An open door between it and the marker within its Move: Move to it, close it and lock it (Interact). No such door (in the open): skip this line.
Otherwise: Move to its task and Interact.
reactions: Unactivated: when shot at, Move away.

behaviors.name: Automated
behaviors.summary: Permanent Overwatch on its field of fire, or triggers on proximity.
engaged: Self-destruct drone with a player model within 2": Self-destruct.
Self-destruct drone: Move toward the nearest player model, twice, ending as close as it can.
Drone with no target within short range: Move to within short range with a target, then Shoot.
Otherwise: Shoot, then Overwatch. A turret only shoots into the field of fire the mission gives it.
alerted: Drone: Move toward the marker, then Overwatch.
reactions: Overwatch: Shoot at every trigger it can, up to two.
Never Unaware: it does not hear noise, and starts on Overwatch.
behaviors.close_combat: Never breaks; it has no melee weapon, so it loses every exchange it is forced into.

behaviors.name: Leader
behaviors.summary: Rallies the most suppressed friend nearby, then acts with its element.
behaviors.investigate: Goes with the nearest element; raises its drill one step while within 6".
engaged: A friend within 6" with 2 or more Suppression: Rally the most suppressed, then take one action from the line below.
Otherwise act as the profile of the nearest friendly element (Sentry if it is alone).
alerted: A friend within 6" with 2 or more Suppression: Rally it.
Otherwise act as the profile of the nearest friendly element (Sentry if it is alone).
behaviors.close_combat: Breaks after a lost exchange if Wounded.

behaviors.name: Handler
behaviors.summary: Independent elite; protects the patron's interests first, the mission second.
behaviors.investigate: Moves to the patron's asset, never toward the marker.
engaged: A player model within 6" of the patron's asset: Shoot it, Shoot it (or charge it, if within its Move).
Wounded or with 2 or more Suppression, and the asset safe or lost: Move away, toward the nearest exit or board edge. It escapes if it leaves the board.
Otherwise: Aim, then Shoot, picking Leaders first.
alerted: Move toward the patron's asset; within 3" of it, Overwatch.
reactions: Overwatch: Shoot at the first trigger it can.
Unactivated: when a player model comes within short range in its sight, Shoot.
behaviors.close_combat: Breaks after a lost exchange if Wounded.

behaviors.name: Attached
behaviors.summary: Uses the profile of the element it is attached to.
behaviors.investigate: As the element it is attached to.
engaged: Act as the profile of the element it is attached to (Tactical if it is alone).
alerted: Act as the profile of the element it is attached to (Tactical if it is alone).
reactions: As the element it is attached to.
behaviors.close_combat: As the element it is attached to.

text: Force: the starting force for the faction (for Task Force Boone, the boarding element: one VAT fireteam and one attached specialist). Name every soldier.
Roster: up to 12 soldiers. Up to 8 deploy on a small mission (chapter 13), 12 on a large one.
Arc: generate the first arc map. The campaign turn marker starts at 1.

turn.text: Choose a node to strike: any revealed node linked to the ship or to a taken node. At Standing 2 or less, command chooses for you: the available node with the highest threat tier (ties: your pick).

Collect income: Requisition equal to the Standing table. Spend Requisition (replacements, recovery, ship upgrades) and Intel (node reveals and mission edges). Pick the support assets Standing allows. Choose the soldiers who deploy from those fit for duty.
Build the node's mission with chapter 13, using its mission type, vessel or environment and threat tier. Play it.
In order: casualties and injuries, prisoners, the grade's rewards and the node's outcome, XP and the citation, then advances.
Each recovering soldier ticks down one turn. Ship upgrades bought this turn are finished. Move the turn marker on; if the arc has run out of turns, it ends.

resources.name: Requisition
resources.text: Buys replacements, faster recovery and ship upgrades. Unspent Requisition carries over.

resources.name: Intel
resources.text: Spent to reveal nodes and to shape a mission before it starts. Gained from data, prisoners and some nodes.

resources.name: Standing
resources.text: Command's confidence in the force. Sets income, support and latitude. At 0 the force is recalled and the campaign ends.

resources.name: Evidence
resources.text: The case that Freespace answers to the Meridian Directorate (decision 9.7). It is never spent.

standing.name: Recalled
standing.text: The force is pulled out. The campaign ends.

support.name: Insertion window
support.text: The mission clock's time limit is 5 minutes longer.

support.name: Signals cover
support.text: The first check-in does not raise the alert track.

support.name: Attached trooper
support.text: One extra Regular soldier from the force's teams deploys on loan. Injuries apply to it, but it gains no XP and returns to command after the mission.

support.name: Intel package
support.text: 1 Intel to spend on this mission only.

intel_uses.name: Reveal a node
intel_uses.text: A hidden node shows its type.

intel_uses.name: Their pattern
intel_uses.text: The first check-in comes at minute 15, not 10.

intel_uses.name: Eyes on a contact
intel_uses.text: At setup, roll one contact chip's result and place that element openly, Unaware.

intel_uses.name: Re-roll the complication
intel_uses.text: Roll the mission's complication again; the second roll stands.

procedure: Draw the ship on the left, then three node boxes in a column, two in the next and the target on the right. Number them 1 to 6, top to bottom, left to right; the target is node 6.
Link the ship to nodes 1, 2 and 3. Link nodes 4 and 5 to the target.
For each of nodes 1, 2 and 3 roll a die: 1–3 link it to node 4, 4–5 to node 5, 6 to both. If node 4 or 5 has no link from the left, link it to the nearest node in column 1.
Roll each of nodes 1–5 on the node table; the target is an operations hub. Column 1 is threat tier 1, column 2 tier 2, the target tier 3.

Nodes 1–3 are revealed. Nodes 4, 5 and the target are hidden: mark them '?' and keep their rolls face down (or roll when revealed). A node is revealed when a node linked to it is taken, or for 1 Intel.
taking: A node is taken when its mission is graded Decisive or Marginal. Collect the node's reward.
A Failure leaves the node standing; its threat tier rises by 1 (to 4 at most). It may be struck again.
A node can be struck if it is revealed and linked to the ship or to a taken node.
end: The arc is won when the target is taken: Decisive if its mission was Decisive, otherwise Marginal. Gain 2 Evidence and 1 Standing.
The arc is lost if the turn marker passes the last turn: the network relocates. Lose 1 Standing. Evidence stays.
Between arcs: soldiers keep XP, advances, injuries and recovery; resources carry over; generate a new map. A campaign is usually one to three arcs.

nodes.name: Relay station
nodes.reward: Reveal every node on the map; +1 Intel.

nodes.name: Forward depot
nodes.reward: +2 Requisition; the next mission's threat tier is 1 lower (1 at least).

special_nodes.name: Operations hub
special_nodes.setting: Roll a die: 1–3 ship (station module), 4–6 land (fortified position).
special_nodes.reward: The arc is won (see the end of the arc).

special_nodes.name: Holding site
special_nodes.setting: As the node where the soldier was captured.
special_nodes.reward: The soldier comes home: roll for injury, +1.

rewards.text: +3 Requisition, +1 Standing. The node is taken.
−1 Standing. The node stands, its threat tier 1 higher (4 at most).
+1 Intel; +1 Evidence as well at threat tier 3 or 4.

casualties: Dead: the soldier's name goes on the force's roll of honour.
Down at any point in the mission, and alive at the end: roll on the injury table.
Left behind Down: captured. A holding site node joins the map, linked to the node where it happened, at the same threat tier, revealed. Strike it to bring the soldier home.
Left behind standing: the soldier makes their own way back and is out for 1 turn.
Wounded markers alone leave no lasting injury.

injury_modifiers.text: The soldier was Bleeding or Critical during the mission
A Medic action saved or treated the soldier during the mission (chapter 7)

injuries.name: Dies of wounds
injuries.text: The soldier dies. Roll of honour.

injuries.name: Crippled
injuries.text: Permanently −1 to an attribute: roll a die, 1 Move (−1"), 2 Shoot, 3 Fight, 4 Physique, 5 Nerve, 6 Tech (0 at least). Out 3 turns.

injuries.name: Close call
injuries.text: Fit for the next mission, and +1 XP.

xp.text: Did the objective's action: took it, freed the hostage, set a charge that destroyed a target, or took the HVT
Put one or more enemy models Down or worse, or made one surrender
The citation: one soldier per mission, your pick, for the deed of the mission (record it)

text: Each time a soldier reaches 5, 10, 15 (and so on) XP, roll a die on the advance table. If the result is already at its cap, choose another row.
Rank follows advances: a Regular becomes a Veteran at 3 advances and an Elite at 6 (a Green soldier becomes Regular at 1). Rank is a label (chapter 1).

table.text: +1 Tech (3 at most), or +1" Move (once per soldier)
A skill: Leader, Medic, Marksman (next level), Scout or Low-light; or choose any row above

honours.name: Medal
honours.text: A soldier with three citations is decorated: +1 Standing (once per soldier), and the name goes on the honour roll.

honours.name: Unit honour
honours.text: A team earns a mark when all its fit soldiers deploy and the mission is Decisive. At 3 marks it takes one honour from the list below, for good.

honour_list.name: Breachers
honour_list.text: +1 to the team's tests to set charges and open or force doors.

honour_list.name: Ghosts
honour_list.text: The first Loud noise the team makes in a mission does not raise the alert track.

levels.text: Out-of-action times are 1 turn shorter (0 at least).
Once per turn, re-roll one injury roll.
Each mission, one soldier may carry one extra gear item from the gear list.
Each mission, one soldier may swap its weapon for an LMG, DMR or AT launcher.
Both of the above for two soldiers each mission.
+1 Intel after each mission graded Decisive or Marginal.
One Intel use each mission is free.
At the start of each turn, reveal one hidden node.

costs.item: Replacement soldier (any troop in the force's teams, 0 XP): Green
Fast-track recovery: one recovering soldier is fit a turn sooner

events.name: Leak
events.text: The enemy knows you are coming: the target's threat tier is 1 higher (4 at most).

events.name: Enemy reinforces
events.text: The next mission's threat tier is 1 higher (4 at most).

events.name: Questions from command
events.text: Lose 1 Standing, unless you spend 2 Requisition.

events.name: Downtime
events.text: One recovering soldier is fit a turn sooner.

events.name: Volunteers
events.text: One free Regular replacement from the force's teams, if the roster has room.

events.name: Opportunity
events.text: A new node joins the map: roll its type; threat tier 1; linked to the ship or to any taken node; revealed.

evidence: Evidence comes from the after-action rewards, safe houses and winning an arc. It is never spent.
At 6 Evidence, the Directorate is exposed: the next arc is against the Meridian Directorate. Its column 1 is threat tier 2, column 2 tier 3, and the target tier 4.

ranks.name: Green
ranks.text: New to the job: crew, conscripts, fresh hires.

ranks.name: Regular
ranks.text: Trained and steady: most soldiers and professional security.

ranks.name: Veteran
ranks.text: Experienced: team leaders, specialists, seasoned contractors.

ranks.name: Elite
ranks.text: The best there is: special operators, intelligence handlers.

shoot_scale.text: Professionals: rangers, Task Force Boone, top-tier contractors.
Elite units: Raid Force Alpha, Delta Force.

attributes.name: Move
attributes.text: Inches per Move action (usually 5-7). Training, exoskeletons and heavy kit all show here.

attributes.name: Shoot
attributes.text: Hit rolls, Suppressive Fire and reaction shots.

attributes.name: Physique
attributes.text: Throwing, forcing doors with a breaching tool, holding on in decompression, getting up when Down.

attributes.name: Nerve
attributes.text: Breaking tests, Find Cover, and initiative for Leaders.

attributes.name: Tech
attributes.text: Medic actions, hacking, putting out fires and other technical work.

attributes.name: Wounds
attributes.text: Wounded markers a model can carry; one more puts it Down.

attributes.name: Size
attributes.text: Physical bulk: 1 small drone, 2 human, 3 large (walkers and vehicles are larger). Used by rules for hatches, cover and vehicles.

hit_modifiers.text: Target in darkness beyond 6" (no low-light gear)

wound_table.text: Wounded: add a Wounded marker. More markers than Wounds: Down
Wounded and +1 Suppression. More markers than Wounds: Down
Down: may recover (end-of-round test 8+, or Medic)
Down and bleeding: dies at end of third round unless Medic 8+
Critical: dies at end of next round unless Medic 10+

factions.name: Task Force Boone
factions.summary: Expeditionary task force whose Void Assault Teams board and clear ships and stations.

factions.name: Galactic Republic
factions.summary: The Grand Army of the Republic: clone troopers, specialists and commandos led by clone officers and Jedi.

factions.name: Anchorage
factions.summary: Near Present: Anchorage Multi-Function Response Company, a US-contracted maritime PMC. Scouts in three-man cells, a Prime and Systems Operators, with a Hound combat robot.

factions.name: Hankou
factions.summary: Near Present: Hankou Advanced Maritime Systems' security force, ex-PNLAN marines in two SPEAR teams with a pair of ZQ44 combat robots.

factions.name: Freespace Solutions
factions.summary: Privatized debt and salvage corporation that unofficially conducts grey-zone operations for paying patrons.

factions.name: Contractors
factions.summary: Mercenary companies and hired guns Freespace pays by the job.

factions.name: UN Force Command
factions.summary: The Authority's regular forces: the professional 3rd Battalion and the augmented Raid Force Alpha, with their inorganic combat units.

factions.name: Meridian Directorate
factions.summary: Technocratic state run through its intelligence ministries; Freespace's current patron.

threat_tiers.name: Low
threat_tiers.summary: Crew and asset security under a recovery captain.

threat_tiers.name: Medium
threat_tiers.summary: Adds collections enforcers, salvage techs and automated defences.

threat_tiers.name: High
threat_tiers.summary: Adds repossession teams, liquidators and hired guns; a contractor reaction force answers high alert.

threat_tiers.name: Story
threat_tiers.summary: Adds Meridian Directorate handlers or deniable operators, or UN Force Command: the 3rd Battalion and Raid Force Alpha.

gear.name: Breaching charge
gear.text: One charge. Place with Interact on a door, hatch or thin bulkhead within 1"; detonate later as an action (chapter 6).

gear.name: Breaching tool
gear.text: Force a locked door: Interact, 2d6 + Physique, 8+ (chapter 3). Also counts as a breaching tool or heavy blade in close combat.

gear.name: Trauma kit
gear.text: The carrier has the Medic skill.

gear.name: Hacking rig
gear.text: The carrier may Hack locked doors and consoles: Interact, 2d6 + Tech against the security level (chapter 3). Quiet.

gear.name: Low-light optics
gear.text: The carrier has the Low-light skill: it ignores the darkness penalty.

gear.name: Extinguisher
gear.text: May Interact with a fire cell in contact: 2d6 + Tech, 8+ to put it out (chapter 8).

gear.name: Silencer
gear.text: The carrier's ranged weapon gains the Silenced keyword: its shots are not noise for the alert track.

gear.name: Jump pack
gear.text: Move ignores the extra cost of obstacles and may cross gaps up to half the model's Move. In zero-g, the model may change direction freely during a Move and stop anywhere, even away from a surface (it still counts as unbraced).

gear.name: Grenade launcher
gear.text: The carrier may Throw frag grenades using Shoot instead of Physique, with a throw range of 18". Its Throws are fired (chapter 6: a natural 2 is a dud), Very loud, and count as Shoot actions for reactions.

gear.name: Ballistic shield
gear.text: The carrier has the Shield skill. It cannot use a weapon with the Cumbersome keyword while carrying it.

gear.name: Jammer
gear.text: Enemy Automated models within 6" take -2 to hit, and enemy Hack tests within 6" take -2.

gear.name: Mk19 grenade launcher
gear.text: Mounted automatic grenade launcher. The carrier may Throw frag grenades using Shoot instead of Physique, with a throw range of 30"; one Shoot action throws two, at points within 3" of each other. Its Throws are fired (chapter 6: a natural 2 is a dud), Very loud, and count as Shoot actions for reactions.

gear.name: Mobility and one-way attack package
gear.text: Climbing legs and a warhead: the carrier crosses obstacles at no extra cost and has Self-destruct 2 (Explosion 3).

gear.name: Flux warhead
gear.text: Once per mission, as an action: an electromagnetic burst. Every Automated model within 6", friend or foe and including the carrier, takes a hit of 2d10 damage, AP 3.

gear.name: Cooperative engagement package
gear.text: Shares targeting data: once per round, a friendly model within 12" of the carrier gets +1 on one Shoot test against an enemy the carrier can see.

weapon.name: Auto
weapon.text: Auto N: may use Suppressive Fire. Shoot or Suppressive Fire may engage up to N models within 3" of the first target, one roll each, -1 after the first.

weapon.name: One per round
weapon.text: May fire once per round, including reactions.

weapon.name: Cumbersome
weapon.text: An extra -1 when firing after a Move; cannot fire as a reaction.

weapon.name: Explosion
weapon.text: Explosion (X): affects every model within X" of the point of impact that has line of sight to it. One damage roll for all (chapter 6).

weapon.name: Confined
weapon.text: +1 wound row to models in an enclosed compartment of 6" x 6" or smaller.

weapon.name: Breach
weapon.text: Can destroy doors, hatches and thin bulkheads.

weapon.name: Silenced
weapon.text: Shots do not count as noise for the alert track.

armour.name: Sealed
armour.text: Protected from vacuum and smoke; resists decompression tests (+2).

armour.name: Heavy
armour.text: Bulky armour. Its weight is already reflected in the wearer's Move.

spine_turn.text: Turn left or right, toward the side with more open board (your choice if equal).

passage_branch.text: A compartment on one side (the side with more open board; your choice if equal).
A compartment on one side and a small room on the other.

junction_branch.text: A small room on one open side.
A side passage (one passage tile) off one open side, ending in a compartment.

loop_door.text: A second door into the other tile. Second doors make loops: more than one way round.

door_state.text: Locked, at the room's security level.

cover.label: Container
cover.piece: A shipping container or crate stack taller than a model.

cover.label: Salvage
cover.piece: A large piece of wreckage or a dismantled engine.

cover.label: Scrap
cover.piece: A pile of scrap, plating or barrels.

cover.label: Scrap
cover.piece: A pile of scrap, plating or barrels.

cover.label: Machine
cover.piece: A heavy machine: lathe, press or fabricator.

cover.label: Reactor housing
cover.piece: A reactor, drive housing or large machinery block.

cover.label: Beds
cover.piece: Medical beds or a treatment station.

cover.label: Equipment
cover.piece: A large piece of lab equipment.

rooms.name: Maintenance access
rooms.text: A crawlway hatch leads off the deck: Size 2 or less only. Missions may use it as a second way in or out.

rooms.name: Escape pod
rooms.text: Enemy models may flee by it: a model that ends its activation here leaves the board.

rooms.name: Secondary airlock
rooms.text: A second way in or out for either side; mission reinforcements may arrive here.

vessels.name: Freighter / ore hauler
vessels.text: Long and plain: a spine of passages with holds off both sides.

vessels.name: Salvage tender
vessels.text: Freespace's own working ships: cluttered bays and workshops, cheap locks.

vessels.name: Corvette / patrol craft
vessels.text: A small warship: tight passages and hard locks.

vessels.name: Station module
vessels.text: A mining or research station section: junction-heavy, with many small rooms. Add 1 to junction branch rolls.

hazards.name: Darkness
hazards.text: Power failure: the whole deck is in darkness (chapter 8).

hazards.name: Zero-g
hazards.text: Gravity is off on the whole deck (chapter 8).

hazards.name: Fire
hazards.text: Place a fire marker in the middle of one compartment: the workshop, salvage bay or life support if there is one, otherwise the one nearest the heart (chapter 8).

hazards.name: Hull breach risk
hazards.text: Every outer wall is hull: a breaching charge or frag that damages it causes decompression (chapter 8).

missions.name: Seize data or cargo
missions.summary: Reach the objective, take what it holds, and get it out.
missions.land: The middle sector of the far row (chapter 12).
missions.task: A model in base contact may Interact to take it: automatic for a model with a hacking rig (data) or Physique 2 or more (cargo); 2d6 + Tech (data) or Physique (cargo), 8+, for anyone else. Data travels with the model that copied it; cargo is carried, and the carrier has −2" Move. If the carrier goes Down, a model in base contact may take it with an Interact.
missions.lockdown: The enemy locks it down: taking the objective now needs two successful Interacts, and a Hack of Secured (9+) first if it is data.
missions.decisive: Objective extracted and no player model Dead.
missions.failure: Objective not extracted when time runs out.

missions.name: Recover personnel
missions.summary: Find a captured friend or a hostage, free them, and bring them out alive.
missions.ship: The compartment farthest from the airlock by route, other than the heart; the heart if there is no other.
missions.land: A sector of the far row: roll a die, 1–2 left, 3–4 middle, 5–6 right.
missions.task: The hostage (unit card: Hostage) starts bound in the objective. A player model in base contact frees them with an Interact. From then on the hostage is a player model: it activates after the model that freed it, every round, and must end each activation within 3" of a player model if it can.
missions.lockdown: The enemy moves the hostage: at the end of the round, the nearest enemy model within 6" of a bound hostage moves it up to 6" toward the enemy's exit, with it.
missions.decisive: Hostage extracted alive and no player model Dead.
missions.failure: Hostage Dead, still held, or not extracted when time runs out.

missions.name: Sabotage
missions.summary: Destroy two targets and get out.
missions.ship: The heart, and the compartment farthest from it by route.
missions.land: Two sectors of the far row: the left and right ones.
missions.task: A model in base contact sets a charge with an Interact (models without breaching charges use the target's own systems: same Interact). The target is destroyed at the end of that round (Very loud), unless an enemy model is in base contact with it then, which disarms the charge.
missions.lockdown: The enemy guards the targets: place one new contact within 3" of each target still standing.
missions.decisive: Both targets destroyed and the force extracted with no player model Dead.
missions.marginal: One target destroyed and the force extracted.
missions.failure: No target destroyed, or the force breaks.

missions.name: Capture a high-value target
missions.summary: Take a named enemy alive and bring them out.
missions.land: The middle sector of the far row.
missions.task: The high-value target (HVT) is the tier's HVT model, placed at the objective with the guard. Take it by overpowering it in close combat, capturing it while Down (chapter 7), or when it surrenders: the HVT tests to surrender (chapter 10) whenever it is Pinned or Wounded with a player model within 6" and no friend within 6". A prisoner moves with a player model in base contact, which halves that model's Move.
missions.lockdown: The HVT runs: from now on it activates first each enemy turn, using the Handler profile's escape line toward the enemy's exit. If it leaves the board, it has escaped.
missions.decisive: HVT extracted as a prisoner and no player model Dead.
missions.marginal: HVT extracted as a prisoner, or Dead (with the body or its data recovered: an Interact in base contact).
missions.failure: HVT escaped or still at large when time runs out.

contact_results.name: False alarm
contact_results.text: Nothing there: crew who fled, a ventilation fan, a stray animal. Remove the chip.

contact_results.name: Booby trap
contact_results.text: A tripwire charge: resolve a frag grenade centred on the chip (2d8, radius 2"). It is Very loud. Remove the chip.

raises.source: Each check-in the clock reaches or passes (a check-in is missed)

thresholds.effect: Contacts move: at the end of each round, every contact moves 6" toward the marker (or toward the player entry if there is no marker), by the shortest route. Unrevealed elements become Alerted when revealed.
Reinforcements: at the end of the round, the tier's reinforcement element arrives at the enemy's entry, Alerted.
Lockdown: the mission type's lockdown happens at the end of the round.

complications.name: Reinforced
complications.text: One more contact than the tier lists.

complications.name: Tight window
complications.text: The time limit is 5 minutes shorter.

complications.name: Hazard
complications.text: Aboard ship, the vessel's first hazard (chapter 11). On land, Night (chapter 12).

rules: The mission sets its size, or the size of the player force does. The size gives the clock die and the time limit.
The clock starts at 0. At the end of each round, roll the clock die: that many minutes pass. Then resolve the alert track's effects, including any check-in just passed.
Check-ins fall every 5 minutes from minute 10 (10, 15, 20 and so on). Each check-in the clock reaches or passes raises the alert track by 1.
When the clock reaches the time limit, time has run out: the mission ends.

placement: Board: a chapter 11 deck aboard ship, a chapter 12 table on land. The mission names the vessel or environment, or roll.
Player force: deploys in the docking passage aboard ship, or within 6" of its edge on land. It extracts the same way: a model that leaves by the airlock or its own edge is out of the mission, safely.
Objective: as the mission type says. Mark it with the objective token (or two).

Guard: roll once on the tier's contact table, rerolling false alarms and booby traps, and place that element openly within 3" of the objective, Unaware. For a capture mission, add the HVT to the guard.

Contacts: place the tier's number of contact chips. Aboard ship, one in each compartment that is not the objective, farthest from the airlock first, then in junctions and small rooms, farthest first. On land, one in each sector of the far two rows that is not the objective's, farthest first, never within 12" of the player edge. If there are more contacts than places, go round again, farthest first. Number them.
Enemy entry and exit: aboard ship, the spine tile farthest from the airlock; a secondary airlock or escape pod is a second enemy exit. On land, the middle of the enemy's edge.
contacts: A contact is revealed when a player model can see it, or ends a Move within 3" of it. Roll on the tier's contact table.
Place the element with its first model on the chip and the rest within 2", in cover where they can be; then remove the chip.
A revealed element is Unaware while the alert track is below 2, Alerted from 2 on. Either way, newly placed models cannot react until the current activation ends.
A contact that moves into sight of a player model is revealed at once.

briefing.heading: Tasking
briefing.text: Mission type, and who gives the order.

briefing.heading: Situation
briefing.text: Two or three sentences: where, who holds it, why now.

briefing.heading: Objective
briefing.text: What to do, where it is, and how to take it.

briefing.heading: Opposition
briefing.text: Faction and threat tier; the guard (known); the number of contacts (unknown).

briefing.heading: Ground
briefing.text: Vessel and deck seed, or environment and table; conditions or hazard.

briefing.heading: Extraction and time
briefing.text: The way out, the time limit and clock die, and the alert track start.

starting_forces.name: Boarding element
starting_forces.summary: One VAT fireteam plus one attached specialist: 6 models.
recommended_gear: One VAT Assaulter carries a breaching charge, the other a trauma kit.
Attach a Pathfinder with a trauma kit if you expect long fights; a Marksman for ships with hangars or long passages.

skills.name: Leader
levels: A Rally made by a Leader, or on a model within 6" and in line of sight of a Leader, removes 2 Suppression instead of 1. At initiative, each side adds the Nerve of its Leader with the highest Nerve.

skills.name: Void-trained
levels: Ignores the unbraced zero-g penalty; may push off and stop at any surface.

skills.name: Medic
levels: +2 to Medic actions; automatically gets a Down model back up.

skills.name: Automated
levels: Never gains Suppression, never tests for breaking, and is not affected by casualty shock or Rally. A wound row of 6 or more destroys it. Attributes shown as a dash are never used.

skills.name: Marksman
levels: An Aimed shot also ignores the Light cover penalty.

skills.name: Deflect
levels: Holding a lightsaber and not Pinned: when hit by a ranged attack it can see, test 2d6 + Fight, 8+, to deflect it (no effect). −1 for each earlier deflection this round. Test each hit of a burst separately.
A deflection on 12 or more sends the bolt back: the shooter takes the hit, rolling the weapon's damage dice on the wound table.

skills.name: Leap
levels: A Move may include one leap, up or down one level (3") or across a gap up to 3", at no extra cost. Drops up to 6" need no falling test.

skills.name: Jedi discipline
levels: Never takes breaking tests and ignores casualty shock. Pinned only at 4 or more Suppression.

skills.name: Twin blades
levels: Fights with two blades: +1 to close combat exchange rolls.

skills.name: Scout
levels: Deploys up to 6" beyond its side's deployment zone, out of enemy line of sight. Scrub and woods are not difficult ground for it.

skills.name: Shield
levels: Carries a ballistic shield or shield emitter: when it has no other cover, it counts as in Light cover against shots from the half of the table it faces.

skills.name: Layered armour
levels: Explosions step one extra row down against it.

skills.name: Laser detector
levels: Laser warning receivers cue its fire: its Reaction and Overwatch shots do not take the −1 for reacting.

skills.name: Augmented
levels: Genetically or cybernetically augmented: +1 to Physique tests, and it ignores the first Suppression it gains each round.

skills.name: Self-destruct
levels: As an action: an Explosion (2) centred on itself, 2d10 damage, AP 2 (chapter 6). Then remove the model. Very loud.
A bigger warhead: Explosion (3). Set off in base contact with a door, hatch or thin bulkhead, it also destroys it, as a breaching charge.

types.name: Scrub, crops, light woods
types.cover: Light, for a model inside it.
types.sight: Models see into and out of it, but not through more than 3" of it.

types.name: Dense woods, jungle
types.cover: Light, for a model inside it; Heavy if it is also behind a trunk or rock (true line of sight).
types.sight: Models see into and out of it, but not through more than 1" of it.

types.name: Rubble, scrap, ruins
types.cover: Light, for a model inside it; Heavy behind standing walls.
types.sight: Use true line of sight; standing walls block it.

types.name: Low wall, sandbags, barricade, fallen tree
types.cover: Heavy, for a model within 1" behind it.
types.sight: Does not block line of sight.

types.name: Hedge, fence, crop row
types.cover: Light, for a model within 1" behind it.
types.sight: A hedge blocks line of sight, except to and from models within 1" of it. A fence does not.

types.name: Wire
types.sight: Does not block line of sight.

types.name: Container, vehicle, wreck, rock, tank
types.cover: Heavy, for a model behind it.

types.name: Building
types.cover: Walls block sight. A model at a window or doorway, or behind a roof parapet, has Heavy cover.
types.move: Through doors (chapter 3); climbing through a window is an obstacle.
types.sight: Through doors, windows and holes only.

types.name: Bunker, reinforced building
types.cover: As a building; its walls cannot be breached.
types.sight: Through firing slits and doors only.

types.name: Crater, ditch, trench
types.cover: Heavy, for a model inside it against shooters outside it.
types.move: Getting in or out is an obstacle.
types.sight: A model moving along a trench is out of sight of models at ground level outside it, unless they are within 3" of its edge.

types.name: Hill, ridge, dune, raised platform
types.cover: Light, for a model within 1" behind the crest, against shooters below it.
types.move: Normal; climbing a sheer face is an obstacle per 3" of height.
types.sight: The crest blocks line of sight between models on opposite sides below it.

rules: Each storey, platform or level is 3" high. Climbing stairs or a ramp costs the vertical distance as well as the horizontal; a ladder costs double the vertical distance.
Height advantage: a shooter a full level or more above its target ignores Light cover from linear terrain, and treats Heavy cover from linear terrain as Light.

Jumping down up to 3" is free. A model that jumps or falls further tests 2d6 + Physique, 8+; on a fail, roll 2d6 on the wound table (2d8 if the drop was more than 6"), stepped down by armour as normal.

noise.text: On land, Loud noise is heard by elements with a model within 24"; Very loud noise by every element on the board.

conditions.name: Rain or wind
conditions.text: −1 to hit beyond 18". −1 to Throw tests.

conditions.name: Fog
conditions.text: Models are seen only within 18" (12" in a dust storm in the desert).

conditions.name: Night
conditions.text: Darkness (chapter 8): models are seen only within 12".
